transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Thank you for seeing me. Um, is it okay if I just jump right in? 

I guess I'm here because... well, there was a bit of a situation at work. I work in human resources, and I was working on a new onboarding launch. At the time, it just felt so bold and, honestly, completely necessary to get things moving. So I sort of pushed ahead. 

I... well, I ended up committing some company money and vendor time before the final approvals were actually in place. It wasn't malicious, I promise, I just really thought I was helping the company move forward. But... now I'm on leave, and everyone is asking what I was thinking. It's incredibly embarrassing. 

I hope you can understand? I just want to figure this out and do whatever you think is best.
Around the time you made those decisions at work, did you feel unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

Um... energized? Yes, I suppose so. Honestly, for the past few weeks, I felt... well, just brilliantly alive. I really felt like I could finally show leadership what HR can be when we're proactive, you know? It felt like such a positive, inspiring thing at the time. 

But, um... I guess... well, I don't want to sound like a difficult person, because I really do pride myself on being a team player, but... there was another side to it. I did notice I was getting suddenly furious if anyone questioned my process. Even over just really small edits or routine budget questions, I would just get so incredibly angry. Which really isn't like me at all. I was just so passionate about the project, but looking back... I hope that doesn't make me sound awful as a colleague. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
During those past few weeks, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Um... sleep? Actually, no, I don't think my sleep changed much. 

I mean, I was definitely eager to get to work in the mornings, but I still made sure to get my usual seven or eight hours. I really try to be responsible about my rest so I can be fully present for my team, you know? I definitely didn't pull any all-nighters or anything like that. 

I... I hope that's okay? I mean, I wasn't doing anything completely erratic with my schedule, I promise. I just felt really focused during the day. Is that... is that a good thing?
During that period, were you more active or productive than usual in starting projects or getting things done?

Um... yes, I suppose I was. I mean, I really wanted to make sure everything was perfect, so I started getting to the office quite early. I just felt this... well, this incredible drive to get things done. 

I was rewriting all the onboarding decks, emailing people constantly, and rearranging our launch plans. I hope that just sounds like I was being a dedicated employee? I really was just trying to be as helpful and proactive as possible. 

But, um, I guess if I'm being completely honest... it might have been a little intense. I found myself walking the floors a lot because sitting at my desk just felt... well, almost impossible, to be honest. It was like my body had a motor in it, just constantly humming and pushing me to keep moving. I didn't want to bother anyone or seem frantic, I just had so much to do. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During that time, did you feel more important, unusually gifted, or especially confident beyond your normal self?

Um... oh, no, definitely not. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I was being arrogant or... or full of myself. 

I didn't feel unusually gifted or anything like that. I mean, I was confident in the work I was doing, but just in a normal, professional way, I think? I always try to stay very grounded and remember that HR is really a collaborative function, you know? It's about supporting the team, not about me being special or more important than anyone else. 

I would honestly hate for anyone to think I was walking around acting superior. I just felt capable of doing my job well. Does... does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm not coming across the wrong way.
During that period, were you talking much more than usual or felt hard to interrupt?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I really just wanted to make sure I was communicating clearly with everyone, you know? Communication is so important in HR. 

But... I guess if I'm thinking back to the meetings during those weeks... I might have been a bit more talkative than usual. I just had so many ideas I wanted to share. I'd be talking about employee engagement strategies, and then I'd sort of realize I was suddenly explaining my ideas for gallery layouts for the new office art, and then I'd jump right into retention metrics. It all felt very connected in my head, I promise. 

I did notice... well, sometimes I could hear myself talking faster than I normally do. And going on a bit longer. I think a few times people almost had to raise their hands just to get a word in and stop me. I feel terrible about that, honestly. I really pride myself on being a good listener. I hope I wasn't being too overbearing? I just got so caught up in trying to share everything I was working on. Is it... is it normal to get a little carried away like that when you're feeling really productive?
During that time, did you believe things that other people said were not true or unrealistic?

Um... no, definitely not. I really hope I haven't made it sound like I was out of touch with reality or anything. 

I didn't have any strange beliefs or think anything that wasn't true. I mean, my ideas were definitely ambitious, and maybe a little grander than usual for our department, but they were all completely grounded in reality. I was just trying to push the boundaries of what we could achieve, you know? 

I would never want anyone to think I was being irrational or... or making things up. Everything I was working on was based on real data and real goals for the company. I just had a lot of enthusiasm for it. I hope that makes sense? I really try to pride myself on being a logical, reliable professional.
About how many days in a row did that unusually energized and irritable period last?

Um... well, it wasn't like a sudden snap or anything. I really don't want you to think I just woke up one day and was acting completely out of character. 

It was more of a gradual thing, I think? It's been building up for... maybe about a month now? It started right around the time this new executive joined the company. He immediately started challenging the onboarding redesign I had spent months perfecting. I mean, I tried to take the feedback constructively, I really did. I always try to be open to new perspectives. 

But I guess... well, I just started feeling a bit more keyed up, and maybe a little more on edge than usual since then. I just wanted to prove that my system worked, you know? So I started working harder, and then I just kept going. Does... does that sound like a reasonable reaction? I mean, a month isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? I just hope I handled it professionally enough.
Aside from being placed on leave, did this period cause major problems in your functioning at work or in other parts of your life?

Um... well, it's a little hard to admit, honestly. I always try to be the person who keeps everything running smoothly, you know? 

But... I guess, yes, it did cause some issues. Aside from being put on administrative leave—which was just awful, I felt terrible about it—I think... well, because of how I handled the launch of my projects, and maybe how I reacted to the conflicts with the new executive... I've sort of lost the trust of the team. 

They, um, they took me off the HR projects I was leading. I really just wanted everything to be perfect, and I pushed so hard for it, but I think I ended up alienating people instead. I'm usually so good at managing relationships at work. It's really embarrassing to realize I let things get that out of hand. I just hope I can repair those bridges when I go back. It's understandable that they'd need to step back from me for a bit, right? I mean, anyone would do that in their position... wouldn't they?
During that month, did you actually feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Um... I wouldn't say euphoric, exactly. That sounds a bit extreme, doesn't it? I really don't want to give the impression that I was, you know, manic or acting inappropriately at work. 

I just felt... really good? Like, for the past few weeks, I felt brilliantly alive, I guess you could say. I just had this incredible clarity that I could finally show leadership what HR could really be, how much value we could add. It was just a really positive, productive feeling. 

But then... well, I guess I did have moments where I'd get suddenly furious if someone questioned me. Even over just small edits to my proposals, or routine budget questions. I'd just feel this flash of anger that they weren't seeing the vision. I always try to be so collaborative, so it was a little out of character for me to be that irritable. I hope you don't think I'm a difficult person to work with? I really do value teamwork, I just... I cared so much about the project, you know? That's a normal way to feel when you're passionate about your work, isn't it?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, or lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

Um... depressed? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm generally a pretty upbeat person. I always try to look on the bright side of things, especially at work. You kind of have to in HR, right? You have to be the positive one for everyone else.

I mean, sure, everyone has bad days where they feel a little down or tired, but two weeks straight of feeling depressed? Or losing interest in things? No, I don't think I've ever experienced anything like that. I always try to stay engaged and keep busy. That's a good thing, right? To just keep moving forward and not dwell on the negative? I really try to be resilient like that.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt unusually energized or irritable like this?

Um... before this past month? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been a hard worker, and I've had times where I was really focused on a big project, but... nothing that felt quite like this past month, where I was just so... intense about it. 

I've always prided myself on being pretty steady, you know? A reliable presence for the team. I wouldn't say I've ever had a time where I was irritable like that with my coworkers before. That's why it was so upsetting to me, because it's just not who I am. I'm usually very good at keeping my cool. 

So, no, I don't believe there was ever another time like this. It's just a one-off thing, I'm sure of it. That makes sense, doesn't it? Sometimes people just get a little too wrapped up in a stressful project, right?

patient.answer:
Um... before this past month? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been a hard worker, and I've had times where I was really focused on a big project, but... nothing that felt quite like this past month, where I was just so... intense about it. 

I've always prided myself on being pretty steady, you know? A reliable presence for the team. I wouldn't say I've ever had a time where I was irritable like that with my coworkers before. That's why it was so upsetting to me, because it's just not who I am. I'm usually very good at keeping my cool. 

So, no, I don't believe there was ever another time like this. It's just a one-off thing, I'm sure of it. That makes sense, doesn't it? Sometimes people just get a little too wrapped up in a stressful project, right?

inference.note: No history of prior manic/hypomanic episodes and no major depressive episodes reported; current episode has lasted about a month with elevated/irritable mood, increased activity, pressured/talkative speech, and marked occupational impairment without psychotic symptoms, narrowing from bipolar disorder to a single manic episode without psychotic symptoms.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first episode lasting about one month with persistently elevated/energized mood and marked irritability, increased goal-directed activity and psychomotor activation, increased talkativeness/pressured speech, and consequential impairment at work including loss of responsibilities and administrative leave. There are no psychotic symptoms and no clear depressive history. Although decreased need for sleep and grandiosity were denied, the overall syndrome is most consistent with mania without psychotic symptoms.
